questiontext.text:
Find the area of the following triangles, giving your answer correct to 2 decimal places were appropriate:

(a) Triangle \(ABC\) where \(A\) has coordinates ({@ax@},{@ay@}), \(B\) has coordinates ({@bx@},{@by@}) and \(C\) has coordinates ({@cx@},{@cy@}).

Area = [[input:ans1]] units\(^{2} \)[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Triangle \(DEF\) where \(DE = {@float(de)@}\) cm, \(DF = {@if integerp(df_in_question) then df_in_question else float(df_in_question)@}\) cm, \(EF = {@float(ef)@}\) cm, and \(D = {@angleD_degrees@}^{\circ}\) as shown in the diagram below (not to scale).

[[jsxgraph height='200px']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-4, 6, 6, -2], axis: false, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); // Point D var p1 = board.create('point', [-2, 0], { name: 'D', size: 0.1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [-10, -10] } }); // Point E var p2 = board.create('point', [p1.X() + {#float(de)#}, 0], { // feed in length of DE here name: 'E', size: 0.1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [0, -10] } }); // Edge AB (has to be horizontal!) var l1 = board.create('line', [p1, p2], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // ----- Construct ray from D through F ------- // define a rotation from bottom left of given angle var t1 = board.create('transform', [{#float(angleD_radians)#}, p1], { // feed in angle D in radians here type: 'rotate' }); // dummy point to rotate var p3 = board.create('point', [p1.X() + 0.1, p1.Y()], { name: '', visible: false }); // rotated dummy point var p4 = board.create('point', [p3, t1], { name: '', visible: false }); // ray var l2 = board.create('line', [p1, p4], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: true, strokeWidth: 2, visible: false }); // ----- Find point F and construct edges ------- // circle from E of radius EF var c1 = board.create('circle', [p2, [p2.X() + {#float(ef)#}, p2.Y()]], { // feed in length EF here fixed: true, visible: false }); // point F var p5 = board.create('intersection', [l2, c1, 1], { name: 'F', size: 0.1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [-5, 12.5] } }); // Edge DF var l3 = board.create('line', [p1, p5], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // Edge AB (has to be horizontal!) var l4 = board.create('line', [p2, p5], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // ----- Labels ------- // Angle var angle = board.create('angle', [p2, p1, p5], { radius: 0.75, name: {#angleD_degrees#}, // feed here the value of angle D in degrees label: { fontSize: 15, strokeColor: '#000000', autoPosition: true, offset: [15, 0] } }); // length DE var txt = board.create('text', [(p1.X() + p2.X()) / 2 - 0.5, (p1.Y() + p2.Y()) / 2 - 0.5, p2.X() - p1.X()], { fontSize: 15, fixed: true }); // length EF var txt = board.create('text', [(p2.X() + p5.X()) / 2 - 0.25, (p2.Y() + p5.Y()) / 2 + 0.5, {#float(ef)#}], { // feed in length EF here fontSize: 15, fixed: true }); // length DF var txt = board.create('text', [(p1.X() + p5.X()) / 2 - 0.5, (p1.Y() + p5.Y()) / 2 + 0.75, {#float(df_in_question)#}], { // feed here the length of DF fontSize: 15, fixed: true }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Area = [[input:ans2]]cm\(^{2}\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

You used the length of \(BC\) as the height but it's not the height.

Worked Solution:

With a question like this, drawing a diagram is crucial. The diagram below shows the details of this scenario.

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-7, 15, 9, -1], axis: true, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); // point A var p1 = board.create('point', [{#ax#}, {#ay#}], { // Feed in coordinates of A here name: 'A', size: 1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [-12.5, -10] } }); // point B var p2 = board.create('point', [{#bx#}, {#by#}], { // Feed in coordinates of B here name: 'B', size: 1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [7.5, -10] } }); // point C var p3 = board.create('point', [{#cx#}, {#cy#}], { // Feed in coordinates of C here name: 'C', size: 1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [-5, 12.5] } }); // Edge AB var l1 = board.create('line', [p1, p2], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // Edge AC var l2 = board.create('line', [p1, p3], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // Edge BC var l3 = board.create('line', [p3, p2], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', }); // foot of heitght from C on AB var p4 = board.create('point', [p3.X(), p2.Y()], { name: '', size: 1, fixed: true, visible: false }); // height var l4 = board.create('line', [p3, p4], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#901B77', dash:2 }); // Right angle symbol var an = board.create('angle', [p2, p4, p3], { radius: 0.75, name: '', label: { fontSize: 15, strokeColor: '#000000', autoPosition: true, offset: [-1000, -1000] } }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Here, we can see that we can draw the height from \(AB\) to \(C\) and using the coordinates of the points we can find the length of the base and the height as follows.

Base \( = {@bx@} {@S1(ax)@} = {@base@}\) units.

Height \( = {@cy@} - {@by@} = {@height@} \) units.

So, Area \( = \frac{1}{2} \times \mbox{Base} \times \mbox{Height} = \frac{1}{2} \times {@base@} \times {@height@} = {@if integerp(areaABC) then areaABC else float(areaABC)@}\) units\(^2\).

When the answer is an integer you do not need the trailing zeroes. Note that the requirement of 2 decimal places says 'if appropriate'; when the answer is an integer or an exact answer to 1 decimal place then you do not need the trailing zeroes.

Worked Solution:

In this question we can use the formula Area \(=\frac{1}{2}ab\sin{C}\) to find the area of the triangle. It is important to identify which value corresponds to each component of the formula, noticing that \(a\) and \(b\) are the sides that make angle \(C\).

In our case, \(a = {@float(de)@}\), \(b = {@if integerp(df) then df else float(df)@}\) and \(C = {@angleD_degrees@}\). So,

Area \( = \frac{1}{2} \times {@float(de)@} \times {@if integerp(df) then df else float(df)@} \times \sin{{@angleD_degrees@}}\)

\(\quad = {@dispdp(areaDEF,2)@}\) com\(^2\).
